IS : 2474 - 1982

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR METAL CLOSURES FOR DRUMS

( First Revision )
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 November 1982, after the draft finalized by the Metal Containers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council. 0.2 This standard has been revised to cover the popular designs of drum closures prevalent in the country. Critical dimensions of the closure components along with the tolerances have been given to facilitate their In this revision, manufacture, interchangeability and proper fitting. 32 mm and 44 mm tapered spout with inner plug and also the screwed-on type brass bung and faucet closures which are not very popular these days have been deleted; instead 44 mm screwed closures which are popular for packing of liquids in drums have been included. 0.3 The choice of the closure depends upon the product being packed in the drum and shall be specified by the purchaser while specifying the drum. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements for metal closures suitable for different types of drums covered in IS : 2552 - 1979t. The following types of closures have been covered: a) Separate neck with inner lid and capseal ( Fig. 1 );
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). tSpecification for st-el drums ( galvanized and ungalvanized

1.2 This standard also covers the use of bung type screwed closures and the tight lid bitumen drum closures but these have not been described here as they have been covered separately in IS : 1784 - 1977* and IS : 3575 - 1977-t. 2. TERMINOLOGY

4. MATERIAL

4.1 Neck - The integral necks shown in Fig. 2 and 3 shall be drawn from the top plate of the drum. The separate neck shown in Fig. 1 shall be drawn to the shape from the same thickness of sheet as the drum top.
4.2 Plug. - Unless, otherwise specified by the purchaser, the plug shall The thickness of be made from the same material as that of the drum. the sheet used for the manufacture of the plug shall be from 0.50 to 0.63 mm. from 0.25 to 0.30 mm 4.3 Capseal - The capseal shall be manufactured The capseal shall be thick tinplate or blackplate or aluminium sheet. lined with paper or rubber latex compound. The rubber latex compound shall be of annular shape and compatible with the contents to be packed. The paper used as washer in the capseal shall be not less than 0.15 mm in thickness and shall have a substance of 105 f 5 g/m" with bursting strength not less than 28 kPa. 5. MANUFACTURE

AND

FINISH

which shall extend up to the cut edge of the capseal or coated with rubber The paper washer and the latex compound lining shall latex compound. be of uniform thickness firmly adherent and free from discontinuities. *Specification for screwed closures from drums. tSpec&ation for bitumen drums. 5.2 In case of screwed closures shown in Fig. 4, the neck shall be pressed and rolled to dimensions; the screw cap shall be pressed, rolled, knurled to dimensions, and the inner seal shall be pressed to dimensions. 5.3 Assembly - In case of the separate neck shown in Fig. 1, the neck shall be well made and secured all round the drum top by welding. There shall be no distortion of the neck due to welding and that the top rim of the neck shall be perfectly in horizontal plane. 5.3.1 In the case of the integral neck, the neck for the closure, shall be drawn to shape from top of the drum as shown in Fig. 2. The top ec& of the neck shall be curled outwards. The curling shall be of uniform thickness and shall be more than two-thirds of the circle and free:from cracks, distortions and other surface defects. 7

c 5.Z.P In case of screwed- closure's shown in Fig. 4, the screwed neck is clinched into the drum top in two operations on a power press. The first operation is perforating the drum. tbp and second the screwtd neck is inserted and clinched in. The sealing compound along the clinching rim , ensures a leakproof joint.

IS : 2474 - 1982 5.3.2.1 The screw cap is screwed on to the screw nozzle by screw cap wrench which takes a firm grip on the knurl provided on the screw cap rim. 5.3.2.2 is filled. 6. TESTS 6.1 The closures shown in Fig. 1 and 2 shall be subjected to the internal The tests shall be carried out after air pressure of 40 kPa for 15 seconds. the closure components with capseal crimped on shall be fitted to the drum top and the leakage shall be tested by immersing the closure in water for 15 seconds. There shall be no ,. sign of leakage at the closures. 6.2 The closures shown in Fig. 3 after assembly on the drum top shall be subjected to an internal air pressure of 109 kPa, for 15 seconds. The leakage shah be tested by immersing theclosure in water `for 1.5 seconds. There shall be no sign of leakage'at+he closures. The inner seal is fitted by inner seal fixing tool after the drum

s', .,.,L,

6.3 The closure shown in Fig. 3 shall be tested by fitting them on the drum top an'd filling the drum to `the capacity with dry sand. After closing the closure the drum shall then be hung upside down and shall be The lever lid shall not given light strokes from the above in fhe centre. come off, which will be noted by the fall of sand from the closures. 7. SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

7.1 Five samples for test shall be drawn at random from each lot of 1 000 or part thereof. The samples thus selected shall first be checked for dimensions, workmanship and finish and then tested with air pressure (see 6.1 and 6.2 ) or sand filling ( see-6.3 ). Any closure failing in any one I or more requirements shall be considered as defective.
